- When sentiment is consistently low (≤0.27) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 2–5% relative to prior peak.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., >75% from 30d mean), model often overshoots and fails to correct; cap forecast at +10% above peak or use 30d moving average as floor.
- If sentiment swings from positive to negative (e.g., 0.80 → 0.00), model overreacts; apply mean reversion to 14d average within 5–7 days.
- When sentiment is high (≥0.77) and price is falling, model often underestimates drop; add 1–3% downward bias to forecast if sentiment >0.77 and price >70.
- For 30d horizon, model frequently misses early downward trend; if last 3 days show >2% drop, forecast should be adjusted downward by 1–2% per day.
- If sentiment is neutral (0.27–0.53) and price is volatile, model overfits noise; use 14d EWMA instead of 30d forecast for correction.
